events.summary: Speaker B presented the prototype: an attractive banana-leaf look and feel base station and an ergonomic banana-shaped remote.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: we made a an attractive base station uh with a banana leaf uh look and feel

events.summary: Speaker B reported two scroll wheels, one for volume on the left and one for channel on the right, with a turbo button underneath.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: We've got the two uh uh scroll wheels here which you know one on the the left for the uh volume

events.summary: Speaker B explained the turbo button lets the user skip past channels quickly while scrolling.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: you can tell it to to skip th past channels that you quickly

events.summary: Speaker C said pressing the turbo button when the banana is held switches the TV on.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: If you take the banana as such and uh you press the turbo button

events.summary: Speaker B said the same button is a teletext button, and then the scroll wheels browse teletext.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: This is a teletext button. So once you press that then you get teletext

events.summary: Speaker B reported the base station has a front button that calls the banana.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: we have in the uh in the base station we have the the button at the front for uh for calling

events.summary: Speaker B said the banana leaves act as antennas, giving form and function in one object.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Actually they do. That's that's yeah that's uh that's form and function

events.summary: Speaker C reported the power plan: solar cells and rechargeable batteries, with the base station taking mains power to charge.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: we are having solar cells and rechargeable batteries

events.summary: Speaker B proposed considering health and safety, because a child might try to eat the remote.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: I think a child would try to eat it anyway, so maybe we should consider that

events.summary: Speaker B objected that solar cells may not be needed when there is a recharging base station.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: I don't really know if the solar cells are actually necessary any more if you have a recharging base station

events.summary: Speaker C said the battery lasts about 8 to 10 hours of use, and much longer if left unused.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: Eight to ten eight to ten hours

events.summary: Speaker C decided on the regular chip only, not the advanced chip, because pricing is a factor.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: Pricing is was a factor so that's why we have gone for a regular chip only

events.summary: Speaker D objected that multifunctional buttons that change function in teletext mode look puzzling.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: Maybe the the thing that convince me the less is the the multifunctional buttons

events.summary: Speaker C said the group wants to keep the buttons simple, with few buttons and channel buttons switching to scrolling in teletext.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: Not not many, we we want to keep it simple

events.summary: Speaker A said both scroll wheels could be useful for navigating teletext.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: Well in fact b both will be could be useful, navigating through teletext

events.summary: Speaker D objected that users who want to dial digits need real number buttons.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: And what about people who want to use digits? Butto real buttons?

events.summary: Speaker C reported that the banana's shape limits the surface area for buttons on one side.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: there was a constraint that the surface area which we have on this banana on one side

events.summary: Speaker C said the target is a trendy segment that does not care about buttons any more.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: we are targeting a segment which is which is just very trendy kind of thing

events.summary: Speaker D set the evaluation scale as 1 (true) to 7 (false), since the team wanted an even scale with enough granularity.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: It's from sorry, it's from one to seven

events.summary: Speaker B gave the handy criterion a score of 6 on the 1-to-7 scale, since the scroll wheels beat the current remote.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: I'd give it a six like I'd I think it's probably more handy

events.summary: Speaker B gave the functional criterion a score of 4 on the 1-to-7 scale, against the standard of off-the-shelf remotes.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Yeah. I have to say four

events.summary: Speaker C said the locator is the most important feature for a TV remote and the scroll buttons are cool features too.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: the most important feature which I felt was the locator which is a cool feature

events.summary: Speaker B gave the easy-to-use criterion a score of 7 on the 1-to-7 scale.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Uh, okay, definitely easy to use

events.summary: Speaker D's price-criterion average was about 5.5 on the 1-to-7 scale, given 6 for cheap.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: Six, so it's uh five point five, or less

events.summary: Speaker C estimated the willingness to change remote as about 3.5 on the 1-to-7 scale.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: So it's somewhere three point five I think

events.summary: Speaker A decided to stick to the general feeling of the group rather than summing the scores, since the summed scores lose information.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: we can we should stick to general feeling

events.summary: Speaker A said the production cost must be below 12.5 Euros.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: We should we should be below twelve point five

events.summary: Speaker A decided the group sticks to one battery as the power source.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: Okay so we we stick to battery, one

events.summary: Speaker A dropped the kinetic option and the dynamo, which is charging by shaking the banana.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: No kinetic also. I don't I don't see the difference between kinetic and dynamo

events.summary: Speaker B said the sample speaker is not used; only a simple beep is needed, so the sample speaker was removed from the costing.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: we're not using that, we're just using the the very beep simple beep

events.summary: Speaker B objected that the case is double curved, not single curved, because it curves on two opposite sides.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Well, wait a second, no, it's it's double curved, it's got a c

events.summary: Speaker A decided to stick to plastic, which costs nothing extra in the costing.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: So we stick to plastic, it cost nothing

events.summary: Speaker B asked whether the group should go back to the rubber case, for drop protection.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Well no didn't we say we wanted to do a rubber

events.summary: Speaker A reported the remote has two scroll wheels and three push buttons.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: We have two scroll, and we have three push buttons

events.summary: Speaker B said the group does not need anything special for the buttons, so there are no button supplements.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: No we're not we don't need anything special for the buttons

events.summary: Speaker B said the design is about ten cents over budget, which switching to plastic fixes.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: And then we're basically o on budget except for you know ten cents

events.summary: Speaker C estimated about 0.90 Euros for the cord and the remaining base station parts.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: So might be ninety centimes for the the remaining things

events.summary: Speaker A said extra profit will be invested in R and D.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: Um we'll invest in R_ and D_

events.summary: Speaker B said the team needed a focus group of young trendsetters to play with the banana.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: We needed some of these kind of young trendsetters to come in and play with the banana

events.summary: Speaker A proposed a street evaluation asking young people whether they would like a banana remote.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: we should do a kinda evaluation in the streets like asking to young peoples

events.summary: Speaker B proposed checking the market for young children, with a banana remote for households with a TV per child.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: maybe in some households where there is you know a T_V_ for each kid

events.summary: Speaker B questioned whether the integrated circuit is needed, since the remote has only two push buttons and two scrollers.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: I mean all we have is two push buttons and two scrollers, do we really need an integrated circuit

events.summary: Speaker D proposed a more general remote control instead of focusing on TVs only, with little added complexity.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: So more general remote control instead of just focusing on uh on T_V_

events.summary: Speaker B proposed a version two that controls mood lighting and the room, not just electronics.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: the ability to you know to control things other than the T_V_

events.summary: Speaker A proposed asking the production department for a real prototype to test at home.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: maybe maybe we can hassle the the production department to to make a a real prototype
